blocks.text: B1-21 · The written summary
Lesson overview

Resuming is the skill that brings together all the B1: understanding a text without vowels, distinguishing the essential from the secondary, rewording with own words, connecting ideas with the Connective. On examination B1 you will write an Arabic summary of an Arabic text of about 250 words, 100–120 words; In real life you will sum up articles, meetings, phone calls. In this unit you learn a method in five steps (understand, choose, delete and generalize, reformulate, link), the formulas typical of the summary ( ⁧يَتَنَاوَلُ النَّصُّ⁩ …, ⁧يَرَى الكَاتِبُ أَنَّ⁩ …, ⁧وَيَخْلُصُ إِلَى أَنَّ⁩ ...) and techniques for shortening: indirect discourse, the maṣdar, the general term. Three weeks.

rows: B1 · Module B1.4 "Write, speak, open sources"
Module B1.3, particularly B1-17 (reading without voice) and B1-20 (connective)
18–20 hours · three weeks (weeks 140–142), plus the EGY track

blocks.text: Materials This unit, pencils of two colors, chronometer, voice synthesis scripts, tutorial sessions
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. identify the main idea, the secondary ideas and the conclusion of an argumentative or chronic text;
2. delete examples, quotes, repetitions and secondary details, and replace lists by a general term;
3. Reword with indirect discourse ( ⁧أَكَّدَ أَنَّ⁩ ...) and with maṣdar ( ⁧اِرْتِفَاعُ الأَسْعَارِ⁩ );
4. write a summary in Arabic of 100–120 words, neutral and well connected, with the typical formulas;
5. read in silence a text by 200–250 words at least 65–70 words per minute and summarize it.
Three-week plan.

1. Dialogue 1 · A summary as long as the text
Salmā returns the tasks.

Salmā: Luke, I asked you for a summary of a hundred words, and you wrote three hundred!

⁧سَلْمَى: اِسْأَلْ ثَلَاثَةَ أَسْئِلَةٍ: عَمَّ يَتَحَدَّثُ النَّصُّ؟ مَاذَا يَقُولُ الكَاتِبُ؟ وَإِلَى أَيِّ نَتِيجَةٍ يَخْلُصُ؟⁩
Salmā: Ask three questions: what is the text about? What does the author say? To what conclusion does it come?
Luke: What about the examples? What about the numbers?
⁧سَلْمَى: الأَمْثِلَةُ تَحْذِفُهَا، إِلَّا إِذَا كَانَتْ هِيَ الفِكْرَةَ نَفْسَهَا. وَمِنَ الأَرْقَامِ تَحْتَفِظُ بِرَقْمٍ أَوْ رَقْمَيْنِ، الأَهَمِّ فَقَطْ.⁩
Salmā: The examples are taken away, unless they are the idea itself. You keep one or two numbers, just the most important ones.
What about the quotes? The minister said a nice sentence...
⁧، بِكَلِمَاتِكَ⁩ «… ⁧أَكَّدَ الوَزِيرُ أَنَّ⁩ » ⁧لَا اقْتِبَاسَاتٍ فِي التَّلْخِيصِ. اُكْتُبْ:⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧أَنْتَ.⁩
Salmā: No quotes in the summary. Write: "The minister has emphasized that..." ♪ In your own words.
Luca: And I finally write my opinion?
⁧سَلْمَى: لَا! التَّلْخِيصُ مُحَايِدٌ: تَنْقُلُ رَأْيَ الكَاتِبِ، لَا رَأْيَكَ. رَأْيُكَ لَهُ مَكَانٌ آخَرُ: التَّعْلِيقُ.⁩
Salmā: No! The summary is neutral: report the author's opinion, not yours. Your opinion has another place: comment.

2. What is a summary (and what is not)

rows: shorter: usually a third or a quarter of the text
a shortened translation, sentence by sentence
faithful: the ideas of the author, in the same relationship of importance
a choice of phrases that we like
written in his own words, in the third person

blocks.text: a linked text, which reads itself a list of points

The three applications for Salmā are the heart of the method: ⁧عَمَّ يَتَحَدَّثُ النَّصُّ؟⁩ (the subject) · ⁧مَاذَا يَقُولُ الكَاتِبُ؟⁩ (the main ideas) · ⁧إِلَى أَيِّ نَتِيجَةٍ يَخْلُصُ؟⁩ (the conclusion). A summary that answers these three questions well is already a good summary.
3. Steps 1 and 2: understand and choose

Over 1 · Understand. Read the text twice. The first time without stopping (global reading); The second with the pencil, looking for unknown words only if they are important to the sense. Look at the title, subtitle, first and last sentences, and the connectives (B1-20): show you the structure. Over 2 · Choose. For each paragraph, it highlights in one color the main idea (usually the first or last sentence of the paragraph) and in another color the ideas that support it. Then write in margin, for each paragraph, a short sentence: 1 the problem; § 2 the causes; § 3 the consequences; § 4 the author's proposal is not applicable.

4. Over 3: eliminate and generalize

Eliminate. Take away everything that doesn't answer the three questions. A simple proof: if you remove the sentence, does the meaning of the text change? If not, delete it. Generalize. Replace a list with a general term ( ⁧تَعْمِيم⁩ ):

6. Dialogue 2 · The synthesis of the interpreter
At the police station, Luca asks for advice from Karīm.

rows: ⁧لُوكَا: كَرِيمُ، هَلْ تُلَخِّصُ كَثِيرًا فِي عَمَلِكَ؟⁩
Luca: KarīmDo you often summarize in your work?
⁧كَرِيم: كُلَّ يَوْمٍ تَقْرِيبًا. أَحْيَانًا يَتَكَلَّمُ شَخْصٌ عَشْرَ دَقَائِقَ، وَيُرِيدُ الزُّمَلَاءُ الخُلَاصَةَ فِي دَقِيقَةٍ.⁩
Karīm: Almost every day. Sometimes a person speaks ten minutes, and colleagues want the synthesis in one minute.
⁧لُوكَا: وَكَيْفَ تَفْعَلُ؟ أَلَا تَخَافُ أَنْ تَنْسَى شَيْئًا مُهِمًّا؟⁩
How do you do that? Aren't you afraid to forget something important?
⁧كَرِيم: أَكْتُبُ مُلَاحَظَاتٍ قَصِيرَةً: كَلِمَاتٍ أَسَاسِيَّةً، أَرْقَامًا، أَسْمَاءً. ثُمَّ أَبْدَأُ بِالفِكْرَةِ الرَّئِيسِيَّةِ، قَبْلَ التَّفَاصِيلِ.⁩
Karīm: I take brief notes: keywords, numbers, names. Then I start with the main idea, before the details.
Luca: As on the news: first the title!
⁧كَرِيم: تَمَامًا. وَالقَاعِدَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ: أَنْ أَكُونَ أَمِينًا. لَا أُضِيفُ شَيْئًا، وَلَا أُغَيِّرُ المَعْنَى، حَتَّى لَوْ كُنْتُ لَا أُوَافِقُ عَلَى مَا قِيلَ.⁩
Karīm: Exactly. And the second rule: to be faithful. I don't add anything and I don't change the point, even if I disagree with what has been said.
Luca: What if the speech is ambiguous?
⁧كَرِيم: أَقُولُ إِنَّهُ غَامِضٌ، وَلَا أُخَمِّنُ. الخَطَأُ فِي التَّلْخِيصِ أَخْطَرُ مِنَ الخَطَأِ فِي كَلِمَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ.⁩
Karīm: I say it's ambiguous, and I don't guess. An error in the summary is more serious than a one-word error.
⁧لُوكَا: أَمِينٌ، قَصِيرٌ، وَالأَهَمُّ أَوَّلًا. سَأُجَرِّبُ ذٰلِكَ فِي وَاجِبِ سَلْمَى!⁩
Luke: Faithful, short, and the most important first. I feel it in the task of Salmā!
⁧كَرِيم: وَإِذَا نَجَحْتَ، تَعَالَ اعْمَلْ مَعِي مُتَرْجِمًا!⁩
Karīm: And if you can, come work with me as an interpreter!

7. Over 5: connect and present
The formulas of the summary.

rows: The article points out that... · stresses...
On the one hand, on the other...

blocks.text: conclusion ... ⁧وَفِي الخِتَامِ يَدْعُو إِلَى⁩ · … ⁧وَيَخْلُصُ الكَاتِبُ إِلَى أَنَّ⁩ and the author concludes that... · and finally invites you to...

The shape. The summary is in third person (the text, the author), at this point ( ⁧يَرَى⁩ , ⁧يُؤَكِّدُ⁩ ), in a single block or in two paragraphs. The first sentence says the argument and the source; the last conclusion. Final checklist.
1. Did I answer the three questions (subject, ideas, conclusion)?
2. I have respected the required length (usually one third of the text: 100–120 words for a text of 300)?
3. Are there any examples, quotations or my opinion? (If so, take them off.)
4. Did I use at least three formulas of the summary and four connectors?
5. I've been looking at arrangements, cases later. ⁧إِنَّ⁩ / ⁧أَنَّ⁩ , and the conjunctive after ⁧أَنْ⁩ ?

9. Resumption of an Arabic text in English
In the reading tests (and in the work) they will often ask you to summarize an Arabic text in English. The method is the same, with two extra attentions:
1. Do not translate before and summarize after: work directly on ideas, with notes in English on the margins of the Arabic text.

2. Make Arabic formulas with natural Italian formulas: ⁧يَرَى الكَاتِبُ أَنَّ⁩ • according to the author (s); ⁧يُذْكَرُ أَنَّ⁩ Go Recall that it is not possible to use the word "switches' in the form of "switches'. ⁧أَمَّا⁩ … ⁧فَـ⁩ As for... Names of people, places and entities in the current Italian form (ONO-03).
10. Pronunciation

You're taking it back. In the oral summary (Script B, oral production) the rhythm is slower than that of a conversation: pause after the sentence that says the argument, pause before the conclusion. Use formulas as signals: yatanāwalu n-naṣṣu... (break) wa-yaraa l-kātibu Anna... wa-yaḫluṣu ilā Anna... Shapes with hamza. ⁧يَحْتَفِظُ⁩ , ⁧يَخْلُصُ⁩ , ⁧اِقْتِبَاس⁩ , ⁧إِيجَاز⁩ : attention to ḫ of ⁧يَخْلُصُ⁩ and the ẓ Ethatic of ⁧يَحْتَفِظُ⁩ ( yaḥtafiẓu).
